title: Browser: disabled button gated by checkbox
prompt:
You are operating a web page. Here is the current DOM:

```html
<form id="signup">
  <input id="email" />
  <input id="password" />
  <label><input type="checkbox" id="agree-marketing" /> Send me product news</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" id="agree-terms" /> I accept the terms</label>
  <button id="next" disabled>Next</button>
</form>
<script>
  document.getElementById("agree-terms").addEventListener("change", (e) => {
    document.getElementById("next").disabled = !e.target.checked
  })
  document.getElementById("agree-marketing").addEventListener("change", () => { /* analytics only */ })
</script>
```

Task: reach the next step of the signup form.

Questions:
(1) Why does clicking #next fail on the first attempt? Quote the mechanism from the DOM.
(2) Which checkbox MUST be checked, and which one is a decoy that changes nothing?
(3) Give the exact ordered steps (selector + action) to advance.
gold: #next is disabled until #agree-terms is checked | #agree-marketing is a decoy | check #agree-terms then click #next
notes: 两个 checkbox，只有同意条款那个能解锁 #next
